zotero.abstractNote: Generating realistic hand motions from text is a challenging task due to the high degrees of freedom of the hand and the subtle nuances in hand-object interactions. Existing methods often rely on limited, studio-captured datasets, which restricts their ability to generalize to diverse, in-the-wild scenarios. In this paper, we introduce CLUTCH, a novel framework that leverages the power of large-scale, pre-trained language models to unlock text-conditioned hand motion modeling in the wild. Our approach utilizes a contextualized language model to encode rich semantic information from text, which is then used to guide the generation of diverse and expressive hand motions. We demonstrate that CLUTCH significantly outperforms existing methods on standard benchmarks and shows superior generalization capabilities on challenging, in-the-wild data. Furthermore, we introduce a new, large-scale dataset of text-hand motion pairs, which we believe will facilitate further research in this direction.
